history.dynasty: Maratha (royal patronage of the Bhonsle ruler of Nagpur)
history.period: Founded 16th century; main gate inscribed Samvat 1610 (1553–54 CE)
history.summary: Dudhadhari Math at Mathpara, Raipur is a Vaishnavite math-temple complex founded by 16th-century monk Swami Balabhadradas Ji Maharaj, who lived on milk alone (dudh-ahari), giving the math its name; legend says he anointed Hanuman with cow's milk and drank the leftover, and a cow named Surhi bathed the idol with milk. The main gate bears 'Shri Dudhadhari Math, Samvat 1610' (= 1553–54 CE). It came under the patronage of the Maratha ruler of Nagpur, Maharaja Raghuji Bhonsle, whose royal charter gave the head mahant the title 'Rajeshri' (still used; current head: Rajeshri Dr. Mahant Ramsundar Das Ji Maharaj). The fort-like complex with high walls holds three main courtyard shrines — Ram Janaki, Shri Balaji and Sankatmochan (Hanuman, the presiding deity) — plus an old well and Ramayana/Mahabharata carvings. Date conflicts in secondary sources: gate inscription Samvat 1610 vs sites claiming 'constructed by King Raghu Rao Bhosle in 1610 AD' (inconsistent, since the Bhonsle Maratha presence in the region is 18th century) or 'established by King Jaitsingh in the 17th century' — verify.
